subject: Decision Making
title: John Stuart Mill and Utilitarianism
description: A micro-lesson that makes John Stuart Mill and Utilitarianism usable.

hook.text: Mill said the right choice is whatever creates the most happiness for the most people. Simple, powerful, dangerous.

buildup.text: Utilitarianism turns every decision into a math problem: add up pleasure, subtract pain, pick the highest score.

discovery.text: This logic runs hospitals, governments, and insurance. Triage, policy, and pricing all maximize total benefit.

twist.text: The math can justify terrible things. If torturing one saves a million, utilitarianism says yes. Most people say no.

climax.text: Mill showed that outcomes matter. But pure outcome math ignores rights, dignity, and the value of each individual.

punchline.text: Most good for most people. Simple math, terrifying edge cases.

quiz.question: What is the main criticism of utilitarianism?
options: It can justify harming individuals if it maximizes total happiness
